issues.claim: v3 headline 'log(N_params) baseline collapses 0.43->0.06' and 'net gain +0.72' are artifacts of a data bug: 14 of the 46 analyzed v3 models (incl. all four 70B/72B anchors) have log_n_params silently set to log(1e6)=13.8155 because MANUAL_PARAM_COUNTS_M was never extended for v3 and missing counts are fillna(1).
issues.evidence: scripts/aggregate_results.py:434-435 `meta["n_params_M"] = meta["model"].map(MANUAL_PARAM_COUNTS_M)` then `np.log(meta["n_params_M"].fillna(1) * 1e6)`; MANUAL_PARAM_COUNTS_M (lines 394-407) contains only the 32 v2 models. Verified in artifact results/study_v3/aggregated.csv: llama3.1-8b, llama3.1-70b, llama3.3-70b-it, qwen2-1.5b/7b/72b, qwen2.5-1.5b/7b/32b/72b, qwen3-1.7b/8b/14b/32b all have n_params_M=NaN, log_n_params=13.815511, and composite_benchmark present (e.g. qwen2.5-72b composite 0.968 with '1M params'). analyze_correlations.py:249-253 fits the baseline on agg['log_n_params'] and lines 157-161 use it as the partial-correlation covariate, so the entire v3 partial.csv and the baseline-collapse narrative (paper/main.tex:36 abstract, :571 conclusion; commit 67af48c 'key finding 2') are computed against a garbage covariate. The intrinsic-feature LASSO LOO/LOFO numbers themselves are unaffected (log_n_params is in exclude_exact, analyze_correlations.py:97-101), but every comparison TO the baseline and every partial-rho in v3 is wrong.
issues.proposed_fix: Add true parameter counts for all 26 v3 models to MANUAL_PARAM_COUNTS_M (or fall back to the already-computed n_params_est = 12*L*d^2, or HF safetensors metadata); replace fillna(1) with a hard assert that no analyzed model has NaN n_params_M; regenerate results/study_v3/analysis/* and the paper's abstract/S3/S7 baseline claims.

issues.claim: Architecture metadata leaks into the 'intrinsic feature' matrix under task-prefixed column names and is selected by the headline models: geometry_cka.n_layers is LASSO-selected feature #21 in v3, and raw depth/head/vocab counts survive as features in both studies.
issues.evidence: results/study_v3/aggregated.csv contains geometry_cka.n_layers (cka.py:149 emits it), causality_tracing.traced_layers.{mean,std,max,q25,q50,q75} (tracing.py emits traced_layers=list(range(L)), then _summarise_list turns it into pure depth proxies), causality_knowledge_neurons.n_layers, geometry_weight_norms.n_layers, dynamics_gradient_flow.n_layers, geometry_schatten.n_layers (schatten.py:284), interpretability_activation_sinks.n_layers (activation_sinks.py:361), interpretability_waa.n_layers_analyzed, causality_attention_knockout.{num_layers_analyzed,num_heads}, geometry_tokenizer_efficiency.vocab_size. results/study_v3/analysis/lasso_features.csv row 20: 'geometry_cka.n_layers, coef 0.0115'. results/study_v2/analysis/findings_report.md:90 lists geometry_tokenizer_efficiency.vocab_size at partial rho=+0.77 (a top predictor) and :157 causality_knowledge_neurons.n_layers (rho with log N = +0.75). analyze_correlations.py:97-101 excludes only the bare metadata columns (n_layers, vocab_size, ...), not their task-prefixed echoes. The paper's 'intrinsic metrics beyond scale' claim is partially carried by raw architecture constants.
issues.proposed_fix: Stop emitting count/config echoes into result dicts (or namespace them, e.g. _meta_n_layers) and add a deny-pattern in analyze_correlations.py feature selection: r'(^|\.)(n_layers|num_layers|n_layers_analyzed|num_layers_analyzed|num_heads|vocab_size|sample_size|n_samples|traced_layers)(\.|$)'. Re-run LASSO/partial analyses; report how many top-25 entries survive.

issues.claim: Aggregator-level `.slope` summaries regress per-layer profiles on the raw layer index (np.arange) instead of normalized depth, so every *.slope feature is mechanically scaled by 1/(L-1) and confounded with layer count — the exact bug class fixed inside tasks by #45/#59 but still present in the aggregator, including LASSO-selected features.
issues.evidence: scripts/aggregate_results.py:126-127: `xs = np.arange(arr.size); slope, _ = np.polyfit(xs, arr, 1)`. Two models with identical depth-normalized profiles v(z) get slopes differing by factor (L_a-1)/(L_b-1) (12-layer GPT-2 vs 32-layer Llama -> ~2.8x). Paper/main.tex:246 claims beta_1 is the slope of a fit to the depth-NORMALIZED interpolated profile. results/study_v3/analysis/lasso_features.csv row 30 selects topology_homology.num_loops_h1.slope; dozens of other .slope columns enter the 730-feature matrix. Prior fixes #45 ('slope regressed on normalized depth l/(n_layers-1), not raw index') and #59 acknowledged this exact bias for task-internal slopes.
issues.proposed_fix: In _summarise_list use xs = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, arr.size) (or l/(n-1)) for the polyfit; regenerate aggregated.csv and downstream analyses for v2-replication check and v3.

issues.claim: CITATION: Paper S3.4 (sec:normalization) describes a layer-profile normalization that is not implemented anywhere: 20-point linear interpolation over normalized depth and the 7-vector [v(.25), v(.5), v(.75), beta1, beta2(curvature), z_min, z_max] with z_min/z_max being the DEPTHS of the extrema — the code emits mean/std/min/max/slope/q25/q50/q75 with no interpolation, no quadratic curvature term anywhere, and min/max as VALUES not depths.
issues.evidence: paper/main.tex:236-247: 'linearly interpolate the profile to 20 evenly spaced depths', 'f = [v(0.25), v(0.5), v(0.75), beta1, beta2, z_min, z_max]', 'beta2 ... quadratic coefficients', 'z_min, z_max are the normalized depths of the minimum and maximum values'. Implementation scripts/aggregate_results.py:112-133 (_summarise_list): no interpolation (direct positional index int(q*(n-1)) into the unsorted per-layer array), emits .mean/.std/.min/.max/.slope/.q25/.q50/.q75; grep of aggregated.csv shows zero curvature/beta2/z_min-depth columns. The q25/q50/q75 positional indexing approximates v(z) for layer profiles, but the same function is applied to non-layer lists (per_head_impacts, degradation curves) where 'q25' is then an arbitrary positional value mislabeled as a quantile.
issues.proposed_fix: Either rewrite S3.4 to describe the actual 8-summary scheme (and rename qXX to v_at_depth_XX for layer groups), or implement the described interpolation + beta2 + extremum-depth features in _summarise_list and regenerate. State explicitly that min/max are values, not depths.

issues.claim: CITATION: Paper states the dependent variable is 'the mean of min-max normalized accuracies across all six benchmarks', but composite_benchmark is computed as the skipna mean over ALL 67-78 benchmark_* columns, 62 of which are MMLU (overall + 4 category aggregates + 57 subtasks, i.e. MMLU counted three times over) — the actual Y is ~92% MMLU-weighted; additionally in v3 per-model benchmark coverage differs (67 vs 76-78 columns), so different models' composites average different benchmark sets.
issues.evidence: paper/main.tex:351: 'composite benchmark score: the mean of min-max normalized accuracies across all six benchmarks.' scripts/aggregate_results.py:559-570: `bench_cols = [c for c in aggregated.columns if c.startswith("benchmark_")] ... composite = bench_matrix.mean(axis=1, skipna=True)`. Column dump of results/study_v3/aggregated.csv: 78 benchmark columns of which 62 are benchmark_mmlu_* (mmlu_acc + humanities/stem/social/other aggregates + 57 subtasks). Coverage check: all v2 models + the four 70B anchors have 67 columns; llama3.1-8b and qwen2/2.5/3 small-mid models have 76-78 (extra boolq/copa/openbookqa/sciq/commonsense_qa/triviaqa/nq_open/gsm8k/drop/truthfulqa/lambada), so composite mixes different benchmark sets across the 46 analyzed models. analyze_correlations.py reads composite_benchmark directly (lines 119-120), so every headline R^2 targets this MMLU-dominated, coverage-inconsistent Y.
issues.proposed_fix: Compute the composite from a fixed declared benchmark list (the six group-level scores: arc_challenge, arc_easy or hellaswag, piqa, winogrande, mmlu_acc, lambada/...), excluding subtask and category duplicates; require identical coverage or document imputation; regenerate analyses; align paper text with whatever is implemented.

issues.claim: The force-eager attention switch in core.evaluate is unreachable when no cache-candidate task is in the run: it is nested inside `if cache_tasks:` and `if cache_num_samples > 0:`, so a selective run of only the 5 non-cache attention tasks (attention_graph/rank/head_roles/induction_heads/attention_polysemanticity) on SDPA-default models gets attentions=None and the tasks error out.
issues.evidence: core.py:192 `if cache_tasks:` -> :201 `if cache_num_samples and cache_num_samples > 0:` -> :211-219 force_eager computed over diagnostic_tasks and applied only inside both guards. cache_tasks is built only from cache_candidates (hidden/logits/attn-entropy sets, core.py:141-190); none of the other four force_eager_tasks are candidates, so `blme evaluate --tasks interpretability_attention_graph` alone leaves SDPA active; attention_graph.py:102-103 then returns {'error': "Model does not return attention weights..."}. Full study runs always include cache tasks, so published numbers are unaffected; this is a run-configuration trap contradicting the intent of fixes #7/#28 ('eager attn enforced for attention tasks').
issues.proposed_fix: Hoist the force_eager block (core.py:211-224) out of the cache branches so it runs whenever any force_eager_task is in diagnostic_tasks, regardless of caching.

issues.claim: Verified the known signal-handler defect: core.py binds old_handler inside try and references it in finally, so when signal.signal raises (non-main thread) the first task records ValueError and the finally then raises UnboundLocalError that kills the entire evaluate() loop; additionally signal.alarm(timeout_sec) raises TypeError if a task config supplies a float timeout.
issues.evidence: core.py:240-263: `try: if hasattr(signal, "SIGALRM"): old_handler = signal.signal(...); signal.alarm(timeout_sec) ... finally: if hasattr(signal, "SIGALRM"): signal.alarm(0); signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)`. /tmp repro (CPython 3.x, thread target emulating the loop body) printed: "task error recorded: ValueError signal only works in main thread of the main interpreter" then "LOOP-KILLING exception from finally: UnboundLocalError cannot access local variable 'old_handler'"; also `signal.alarm(5.5)` -> "TypeError 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer" while signal.alarm(0) succeeds in non-main threads (so the finally reaches the broken signal.signal call).
issues.proposed_fix: Minimal: before the try, `old_handler = None; alarm_armed = False`; inside try set `old_handler = signal.signal(...); alarm_armed = True; signal.alarm(int(timeout_sec))`; in finally `if alarm_armed: signal.alarm(0); signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, old_handler)`. (alarm_armed flag rather than `old_handler is not None` because the prior handler can legitimately be None.)

issues.claim: Residual unseeded sampling sites of the exact class fixed in #42/#50-53 remain in four geometry paths, one of which also makes the no-cache fallback semantically different from the cache path (10 random tokens per sample vs all tokens).
issues.evidence: tasks/geometry/mutual_info.py:62 `shared_perm = torch.randperm(n_tokens)[:max_tokens]` (global RNG; draw depends on how many torch RNG calls preceded the task in the run order); tasks/geometry/intrinsic_dim.py:60 `indices = np.random.choice(len(X), 20000, replace=False)` (global numpy RNG, triggers whenever token count >20000, i.e. standard 100x512 cache); tasks/geometry/isotropy.py:41 `np.random.choice(len(X), size=(min(1000,len(X)),2))` for cosine-pair sampling; tasks/geometry/utils.py:129 `indices = torch.randperm(T)[:10]` in collect_hidden_states single-layer mode — unseeded AND inconsistent with the cache path which returns every token (cache.py:_slice_hidden_states), so geometry_svd/isoscore/lid produce different-distribution inputs depending on cache availability; collect_hidden_states also tokenizes without truncation/max_length (utils.py:90-93) unlike the cache's max_length=512 (cache.py:351-353).
issues.proposed_fix: Use torch.Generator().manual_seed(0) / np.random.default_rng(0) at all four sites; in collect_hidden_states drop the 10-token subsample (return all tokens, matching the cache) and add truncation=True, max_length=512.

issues.claim: set_global_seed omits cuDNN/deterministic-algorithm flags (known-open (g)); assessment: cudnn.deterministic=True + cudnn.benchmark=False are safe to add unconditionally (perf-only cost), but torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) is NOT safe by default — it raises RuntimeError on nondeterministic CUDA kernels (scatter/index ops used by several tasks) and needs CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 — so it should be opt-in with warn_only=True.
issues.evidence: src/blme/utils.py:17-28 sets only random/np/torch.manual_seed/cuda.manual_seed_all. PyTorch docs: use_deterministic_algorithms(True) errors on ops without deterministic implementations and requires CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG for cuBLAS >= 10.2; tasks use index_put/scatter-style ops (e.g. np.add.at analogues, ablation index assignment) on GPU in study runs. PYTHONHASHSEED is also unset but no result-bearing code depends on hash ordering.
issues.proposed_fix: Add to set_global_seed: torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic=True; torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False; and behind an opt-in env flag (e.g. BLME_DETERMINISTIC=1): os.environ.setdefault('CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG', ':4096:8'); torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True, warn_only=True).

issues.claim: wrapper.py passes the deprecated `torch_dtype` kwarg (transformers 5.2.0 keeps it only 'for BC'), `_resolve_dtype` is annotated Optional[torch.dtype] but returns the string 'auto', and quantization uses the legacy bare load_in_8bit/load_in_4bit kwargs instead of BitsAndBytesConfig; device placement and trust_remote_code handling are otherwise correct.
issues.evidence: src/blme/models/wrapper.py:146-148 sets model_kwargs['torch_dtype']; installed transformers 5.2.0 modeling_utils.from_pretrained: `dtype = kwargs.pop("dtype", None); torch_dtype = kwargs.pop("torch_dtype", None)  # kept for BC` — works today, removal candidate in v6. wrapper.py:50-66 _resolve_dtype returns 'auto' (string) under a torch.dtype annotation. wrapper.py:172-179 legacy load_in_8bit/4bit kwargs. Device handling verified sound: device_map takes priority (163-165, 187-188), .to(device) only when device_map unset, quantized loads force device_map='auto'. trust_remote_code applied symmetrically to tokenizer (122-123) and model (151-152), default false.
issues.proposed_fix: Pass `dtype=` instead of `torch_dtype=`; annotate _resolve_dtype -> Union[torch.dtype, str, None]; build a BitsAndBytesConfig for quantization; optionally warn when max_memory is supplied without device_map (transformers ignores/errors on it).

issues.claim: cache.get_hidden_states docstring still asserts per_sample=True 'is what CKA, RSA, LID and matrix-entropy need' while the shipped CKA/RSA/LID consumers deliberately use the flat token cloud (which is correct for CKA/HSIC and conventional for LID/TwoNN) — a stale doc from fix #1 that invites a future 'fix' silently changing locked v2 numbers; separately RSA's max_tokens=200 means its RDM is built from only the first ~1-2 wiki passages.
issues.evidence: cache.py:100-105 docstring vs cka.py:48, rsa.py:55, lid.py:124/143 all calling with per_sample default False; cka.py rows stay aligned across layers because populate() concatenates in sample order, so token-level linear CKA is valid; rsa.py:71-72 `n_tokens = min(min_tokens, max_tokens_per_layer=200)` takes the FIRST 200 tokens of the flat cloud — at 128-512 tokens/passage that is 1-2 documents, and the token span covered differs per tokenizer.
issues.proposed_fix: Update the docstring to name only the consumers that actually require per_sample (matrix_entropy, schatten, get_prediction_stats); for RSA either sample tokens uniformly across all cached samples (seeded) or raise max_tokens, and document the token-level (not stimulus-level) RSA departure from Kriegeskorte 2008 in the task docstring.

issues.claim: Test matrix gaps: conftest's DummyTokenizer ignores the input text, returns unseeded random ids of fixed length 8, and does not implement return_offsets_mapping — so the offset-based code paths guaranteed by fixes #34 (score_continuation) and #49 (WEAT word positions) are never exercised (only their slow-tokenizer fallbacks), and tests are nondeterministic; the CI py3.9 leg cannot install transformers 5.x (study version) so it tests a different major version; blme.list_tasks() returns [] after `import blme` until evaluate()/CLI calls _register_all_tasks (API-only footgun — CLI and tests register correctly).
issues.evidence: tests/conftest.py:204-238 DummyTokenizer.__call__ ignores `text` content and **kwargs (no offset_mapping key, torch.randint with global RNG, length=8); tasks/common.py score_continuation's primary path requires offset_mapping, so tests cover only the prefix-length fallback; .github/workflows/test.yml:14 matrix includes 3.9 while pyproject pins transformers>=4.35 and the study ran on 5.2.0 (requires py>=3.10), so Qwen3Next/Qwen3.5 arch fixtures silently skip on that leg; registry: core.py:33-40 _register_all_tasks is called by evaluate(), cli._cmd_list_tasks (cli.py:128-131) and tests/test_completeness.py:10, but src/blme/__init__.py re-exports list_tasks without registering.
issues.proposed_fix: Give DummyTokenizer a deterministic hash-of-text id mapping, a seeded generator, and a minimal offset_mapping implementation (cumulative char spans); add one test using a real GPT-2 fast tokenizer (cached fixture) for score_continuation and _find_word_token_position; either drop py3.9 from the matrix or pin a transformers version per leg; call _register_all_tasks in blme/__init__ or document the lazy registration.

issues.claim: results.py hygiene: save_results always writes a fixed 'results.json' (silent overwrite of prior runs in the same dir), json.dump emits non-RFC8259 NaN/Infinity literals (tolerated by the in-repo aggregator but brittle for external consumers), and print_results_table assumes every task result is a dict ('error' in result raises TypeError otherwise).
issues.evidence: src/blme/results.py:172-177 fixed filename + json.dump(..., default=str) with default allow_nan=True; :107-110 `if "error" in result` on arbitrary task return values. Aggregator side verified clean: 0 absolute-layer-index columns survive in results/study_v3/aggregated.csv (fix #36 holds), no all-NaN columns, no merge-collision suffixes; remaining naming oddity is float-keyed columns like consistency_position_sensitivity.nll_at_0.25 (harmless — feature_metadata's split('.')[0] still parses the task).
issues.proposed_fix: Timestamp or model-slug the results filename (or refuse to overwrite without --force); guard print_results_table with isinstance(result, dict); optionally json.dump(..., allow_nan=False) after converting NaN->None for strict JSON.

No call site mixes per-sample math with the flat cloud; the two per_sample=True users are exactly the two tasks whose papers demand per-sentence matrices.
